proposals: GSTN should publish SGST collected on ethanol, by state and by year, so state revenue from ethanol blending is an official figure rather than a proxy that no state finance department currently publishes.

PPAC should publish state-wise petrol sales in litres and the volume of ethanol actually blended in each state, so estimates do not have to rest on a 0.74 kg/litre density conversion and an assumed uniform 20% blend.

The GST Council secretariat should prepare and publish a state-wise estimate of petrol VAT foregone because of ethanol blending before any vote on ethanol’s GST rate or its CGST:SGST split, so states vote knowing figures like Tamil Nadu’s small gap and Maharashtra’s large one.

Oil marketing companies should publish their weighted-average ethanol procurement price for each supply year in the same release as blending volumes, so revenue models use the actual price rather than a fixed ₹60/litre assumption.
